quest.title: A Riddle Amidst the Crowds
quest.description: Even though the clues are few and vague, you and Sucrose continue to work at uncovering the mystery behind the prophecy...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Wait until the appointed time (08:00 – 12:00 two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sucrose, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler, Paimon! I only just arrived myself, so I'm still getting ready.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, and Collei just passed by a moment ago. She said she had some things to sort out at the inn where she's staying, but she'll meet up with us when she's done.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Apparently, Tighnari and Cyno both went out, but she stayed behind because she wanted to help us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Understood. How has progress been on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Not too bad. After reviewing it again with fresh eyes, I came up with a new theory which seems to hold some water. I'll attempt to explain it as simply as I can...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I believe that each of the four things in the prophecy refers to a different field of knowledge. So in a way, the prophecy is a test of the reader's intelligence...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But it's unlikely for any one person to have expertise in all these different areas, so I suggest that we seek out one expert from each and get their opinion.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Also, in two out of the four areas, the prophecy seems to want us to find specific people. It may even turn out that the people themselves are the answers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, so it sounds like we should put our heads together and list out the people who can help us!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Exactly. I think we can go through each riddle in turn and generate four groups of names to match the four questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's start from Group 1! The first riddle was... "a flower that is not of this world."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Personally, I would still go with Albedo for this one. Alchemy is the most likely to have to do with otherworldly things, and he is by far the leading expert in this regard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You'd count as an expert too, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! You're the creator of the Tetratanic Sweet Flower. Who knows, maybe that's the flower we're looking for!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh? You really think so? Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, but what about Tighnari? He's a Forest Watcher and knows all about plants. If it's a flower we're looking for, maybe he's the man for the job!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll add him to the list as well.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: On to Group 2. This subject is... "a guide who will never get lost."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's kind of abstract... Does it just mean someone who never loses their way?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Wait, but they have to be able to guide others, too, so it's not quite as simple as that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps... an astrologer, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Mona? Yeah, she'd definitely count!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Mona... Yes, she certainly seems very confident, and she can use her astrology to guide people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Would Bennett count?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Why him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, his luck's so bad that as long as you go in the opposite direction from him, you'll always be going the right way, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm, I see... I—I suppose I can't argue with that logic...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Add him to the list! Finding everyone won't take long, so one extra person won't hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, I know! Would Outrider Amber be a valid candidate for this category as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, she would! She's got a great sense of direction, after all. As a matter of fact, when the Traveler and Paimon first came to Mondstadt, she was actually the one who gave us directions.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes, she's certainly a good guide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Let me think... Ah yes, I believe there may be one more.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Albedo once made a set of equipment for Mika from the Reconnaissance Company. He's their surveyor, and an exceptional pathfinder.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: He's even instructed others in the discipline of surveying before. So in my view, he's highly unlikely to lose his way and would be very good at helping others find theirs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool. Another one for our list.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: ...Wait, Collei should've been here by now. Wonder what's taking her so long? ...Sorry, could we continue our chat somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you wanna go see how she's doing, right? Sure, let's all go!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hi Collei, hope we're not intruding or anything... Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah! Sucrose! I, uh... I was preparing some... stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Is it time already? Oh no, I—I'm sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Collei seems to be wrapping gifts, and now she's frantically trying to hide it. I wonder who they're for?)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Don't worry, the Traveler and I only just met up. We were just worried that you might get lost along the way, so we thought that we'd come get you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'm ready to join you now! Um, how's that thing going?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sucrose tells Collei about the four riddles and the results of your discussion...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So let's pick up where we left off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Next up is the third line: "one who would never lie"... Hmm, anyone spring to mind?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe... Diluc?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... you really think so? Seems like it would be pretty difficult for someone in his position to avoid having to lie.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ah yes, his secret alter ego: the Darknight Hero. He must have to deny it if anyone asks. In that sense, he has a complicated relationship with the truth.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Then what about Kaeya? He's the Cavalry Captain and a rather popular figure, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You think there's something fishy about him too, huh? Yeah... he's definitely a sneaky one! Bet he lies all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Hmm, I can't help but agree with you there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's the Tone-Deaf Bard... Uh, but on second thought, he wouldn't qualify either. He talks way too much nonsense. Hmm... is there anyone else we're missing?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Acting Grand Master Jean? She has a good name in that regard... but from what I know, she sometimes covers up the truth out of concern for those around her...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: For example, when Lisa loses track of time in the library and misses her patrol shift, Jean'll come up with some excuse, like "Lisa's ill today."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Also, she sometimes makes up stories to get Klee to behave. Like the one about the big monster that comes to catch naughty kids who don't go to bed on time... D'you think that rules her out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, white lies are still lies... But do we really have to reject her because of some harmless fibs? It's not like she had evil intentions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This prophecy seems very strict...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, we're the ones being strict!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Rosaria doesn't strike me as the type of person to lie.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah Collei, you probably haven't met her yet, have you? She's a sister from the church who looks, um... a little scary and not very sociable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What gives you that impression?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: She stopped by the alchemy bench once, a long time ago, and asked me about Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I thought maybe she was trying to find him, for work or something. But when I asked, she just said that she was curious about him because he was so intelligent, and wanted to talk to his assistant to find out what he was like.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: A lot of people might have given a more tactful justification, but I could see in her face that she wasn't trying to hide anything. She was just very direct and straightforward.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That's why I don't think of her as the lying type.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rosaria doesn't look like the sort of person you'd want to get into a fight with... Maybe she just fights her way out of situations that some people might lie to get out of?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I can definitely see that! I've also heard the other sisters say that Rosaria doesn't even make excuses when she skips choir — she just doesn't show up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's a tough cookie, huh. Let's put her name down.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: In that case, I think Cyno fits in this list, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, true. Lying's probably more trouble than it's worth for someone like him — kinda like with Rosaria.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and Paimon also nominates Razor! Bet he couldn't lie to save his life.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I've also got someone else in mind, Noelle, the trainee knight! She's a very honest person. I don't think she'd tell a lie.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alrighty, write her name down too!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: ...Wait, there's one more person... You know, our long-standing staffer at the alchemy bench...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean... Timaeus?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes, him. Um, truth be told, he's been lovestruck recently.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: He swore that he wouldn't say a dishonest word or slack off until he succeeds in getting the woman he loves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Timaeus has a crush!?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, who is it? Do you know her?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I've never met her. All I know is that she's from Liyue... Timaeus says that she's fun, has a great personality, and is very, very good-looking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All great qualities, but that says nothing about her identity...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Since we're on the topic — helping Timaeus win the lady of his dreams was also one of my goals for this Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But how can we help with that?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I dunno, make sure he uses nice paper and a fancy envelope when he sends letters to her, help him pick a nice gift and wrap it properly... That sort of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah! I had the same situation once in the Avidya Forest. I helped another Forest Ranger out by delivering a love letter to the coworker she likes...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yep, that sort of thing, exactly! Oh, also, I helped him with some of the groundwork for one of his research projects. He must have appreciated it, because he gave me a refrigeration device that he's been developing as a thank-you gift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it any good?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Uh... I mean, it looks nice...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Sounds like a "no."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, alright, guess we'll put lover boy down on the list then.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Okay, so last of all, we have "a legend that never ends." Anyone come to mind for this particular line?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lisa, perhaps? A librarian understands books best... and aren't most legends written down somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not necessarily, but you have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: When I think about "legends," fairy tales and picture books come to mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe Collei! She read a lot of fairy tales when Tighnari was teaching her to read.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh... Do I count?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Of course you do. I'll put you on the list.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you eligible for this one, Sucrose?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I prefer to read things like "An Illustrated Analysis of Alchemical Substances and Their Uses," "The Fascinating Principles of Crafting," and "Hypotheses of Life"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Point taken... Paimon didn't quite understand any of those...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmmm. Klee might be a good choice. Her mother, Alice, is a renowned traveling author, so I'll bet she's been exposed to all sorts of myths and legends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then, Klee makes the shortlist!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Well, that should just about do it. Next up, we should go and ask the people on the list about the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Do we have to ask absolutely everyone on the list? It seems like a lot of people...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It is, so I was thinking that perhaps we should split up? That might make our search more effective.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okie-dokie!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Also, I've thought of a method of gathering feedback...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sucrose shares her idea with everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem, we can do that.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #You and {NICKNAME} are practically joined at the hip, so you two can go together. I'll pair up with Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Capable Collei and Sensible Sucrose... sounds like a winning combination!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Okay, I promise I'll help! Capable Collei... yeah, I got this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Rest assured that the unbeatable {NICKNAME} and Paimon will do our part too! Off we go!

talks.objective: Go to the library and find Lisa

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I plan on starting from the person with the most defined stronghold, so let's go to the library. Lisa should be there.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "Stronghold," That's an, uh... interesting word to use.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Umm... maybe "den"? No, that's even worse...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: How about... "lair"?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Here we are! Lisa's lair!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Oh no, that was a bad word choice. Now Sucrose is using it and it's all my fault...)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Lisa, might I ask if... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sucrose? Collei? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I can only "Sucrose" that they were "Collei"-ng in on someone. At "Lisa," that's as far as "Cyno."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Please... Just stop it with these puns, I beg you. Are you trying to win worldwide fame for unfunny jokes?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um, is Lisa not here at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Surprising, isn't it? She went out. I'm afraid it's just us here looking for information.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Except me. I'm not here for information. Like you, I came here on an abortive search for the librarian, who is also my Akademiya senior.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, so you studied in the same Darshan as Lisa?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right. Her mentor in Sumeru was also my benefactor. We were both Spantamad students.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Wow, that's cool... But wait, we're getting sidetracked! We came here to look for some information — Collei and I are investigating a prophecy, and we were hoping you all might be able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh? What sort of prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sucrose and Collei take turns explaining the prophecy and the information that they compiled with the Traveler...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I see... You want to ask them about the "flower that is not of this world," and me about the "one who would never lie."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But there's no rush! You don't need to answer right away! We're just here to tell you about the situation. You can take your time to think it over, and submit any thoughts you have in written form to the Sucrose Mailbox.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Sucrose Mailbox?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yep. I was thinking about it on the way, and although these seem like trick questions, there's a lot to mull over once you get down to the details. A quick answer off the top of your head might not go into enough depth.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So, I decided to place a mailbox next to the alchemy crafting table. Everyone can submit their written answers there when they're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: We don't have to call it the Sucrose Mailbox, though. It could just as well be called the Sucrose and Collei Mailbox, or even the Sucrose, Collei, Traveler, and Paimon Mailbox...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Haha, I think in this case, we CAN just go with your quick answer off the top of your head...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sounds like a good solution. Certainly more reliable than verbal discussion alone.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Agreed. Certainly when it comes to discerning whether someone is a liar or not, you cannot simply take them at their word.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Understood. Once we've had a look into it, we'll place our replies into your mailbox.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you all so much. Okay, let's tick them off the list, and carry on working our way down...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Already done.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm pleasantly surprised to see those two introverts getting along so well.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you get the feeling that Collei's return to Mondstadt has emboldened her more contrarian side?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, I'd noticed that too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Traveling and meeting old friends are both good for the body and soul.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And isn't rediscovering one's youth while revisiting old haunts a worthwhile pursuit?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...When I first met Collei, she'd never known happiness or youth.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But things are different now. Her Eleazar being cured was a huge milestone in her life.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei is a very sensitive and introverted child. I'm sure you must have noticed that too, Albedo.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: From the time she's been in my care, I've observed that she's actually a very lively character by nature... but she had a very rough start in life, and it changed her.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So might I assume that your respective claims of looking for plants and artists in Mondstadt were just pretexts?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I wouldn't say that. Both Collei and Genius Invokation TCG are very important to me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Would it really kill you to just say "yes" in this situation?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Fine. Yes, we came out of concern for Collei. She's been back to Mondstadt of her own accord several times, but it has led to no significant improvement in her mood.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, it won't hurt to give her some more time. I believe that Sucrose might be able to help her.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sounds like an extension of your own self-confidence as her teacher.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You could say that. In a similar vein... I've heard that Sumeru's scholars often build their social relationships based on their academic ones. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I suppose it might look like that from your perspective. Sumeru's society is something of a special case — the reason it is known as the city of learning is because all of its resources are in some way linked to academia.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As such, academic resources equate to social capital. It is not unheard of, for example, for people to build a family in order to pursue further studies.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But the relationship between the three of us is not an academic one turned social. We've never even worked on a paper together, for starters.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, so the academic paper is the nexus of the academic family? Interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I would think of us more as siblings. An equal and pure relationship, unaffected by academic considerations.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: As much as I'd prefer not to admit it, that statement is not inaccurate.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I can understand that position. I have a younger sister myself, and it's only natural for me to be protective of her.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What you described fits the idea of a city of learning as I imagine it. The family is where all social relationships intersect... as such, a family founded on common goals may actually be more stable.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: By the way, who's the eldest between you?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's not go down this rabbit hole, please.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: In terms of age, I'm the eldest, of course. He just doesn't want to admit it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But your mental age is younger than that. I daresay even by enough to be the youngest sibling. Perhaps I could bring Collei into this happy family to be your elder sister?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No... You will never see me admit to being the youngest sibling! Except perhaps as a last-ditch effort to turn the tables in a game of cards.

talks.objective: Find candidates that match the prophecy

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we'll leave Collei and Sucrose to it. Fingers crossed all goes well for them! Now then, where should we go first?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's try our luck at the bulletin board, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A lot of people tend to show up there at some point in the day — maybe we'll get lucky!

talks.objective: Head to the Mondstadt bulletin board

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! Just as we hoped, there's a load of people here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Even Lisa's here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hi everyone, long time no see.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: #Hey there, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! It's been a while. How've you been?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been doing pretty well!

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: You look surprised, cuties. Is it because of me?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Teacher is... not at the usual place.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Oh please, it's not as if I'm glued to my chair. I like to get out for a little fresh air every once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Mika's here today, so I thought it'd be a good time to introduce him to Bennett and Razor. They're all out and about quite often, so it's helpful for them to get to know one another.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Mika.

choices.text: Hi, Mika. Good to see you again.

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: I—I look forward to working with you...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: No need to be so formal! We've known them for ages, they're cool!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Windblume... fun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, we haven't gotten to the fun part yet! We've been busy investigating a prophecy.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: A prophecy? What kind?

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: A good one, or a bad one?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain the prophecy and tell everyone what you've learned so far...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Gosh, that all sounds quite fascinating.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I can't believe I made it onto your list of names... You really think I'll be able to help?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Believe... in yourself!

response.speaker: Mika
response.text: Right, believe in yourself! You're a first-rate adventurer, Bennett.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Okay, then in that case, I'll step up and present my thoughts on the matter! ...Uh, except I forgot I'm not really good at organizing my thoughts... Oops...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to tell us all of your thoughts right here and now! Sucrose said she'll put a mailbox next to the crafting bench, so you can just write down your thoughts when they come to you, and drop them there.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: A meticulous and efficient plan. Yep, that sounds like Sucrose.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I will think also. Give me some time.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: You still have other people on your list that you need to go see, right? We should leave you to it! Don't worry about us, we'll drop off our letters at the mailbox as soon as we're done.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Bye for now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head over to Starsnatch Cliff next! Maybe we'll be able to find some people there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And even if we don't find any familiar faces... You can see really far from up at the top. Maybe we can find people that way!

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Aw, you're working so hard. Do be sure to get some rest when you can. If you get tired, you know you're always welcome to visit me for a break and a cup of tea.

choices.text: Hello, Mika. Nice to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Where to next...? Let me check my notes... Ah, this way!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Got it! Collei, please follow me.

talks.objective: Find someone that matches the prophecy

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, it's our lucky day! There are several people over there.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Amber!? Wow, and Eula's with her too...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, it's Sucrose! And Klee also spies... the girl with the long scarf!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Collei, we were just talking about you! Ah, right, I don't think you've been introduced to Noelle before. Collei, this is Noelle, maid of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, Collei. I missed you the last few times you were in Mondstadt, so I'm glad to finally meet you in person.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh... N—Nice to meet you too, Noelle! My name is Collei... but you already knew that.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Relax, you two. There's no need to be so courteous — we're not on some kind of diplomatic mission here.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Klee, what are you doing here? Are you planning to blast some fish?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Nope! Klee's on patrol with the other knights.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh, now that you mention it, it looks like everyone here's a Knight of Favonius except for Collei and me...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'd heard that there was a very young knight in the ranks, but it's still a surprise to see with my own eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Collei, what do you do?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm a Trainee Forest Ranger in the Avidya Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Trainee...?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It means I'm not officially a fully qualified Forest Watcher yet. I'm still learning.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Oh, you're just like me! I'm still working towards becoming a fully qualified knight.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Technically, though the distinction is hardly relevant right now. This isn't a very formal patrol... we're just chatting.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Whew... Don't panic, Collei, just pick a topic and join the conversation! Don't panic, whatever you do, don't panic... It's just Amber and her friends. There's no need to be nervous...)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Let me guess... were you chatting about the new guests in town?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yep! A few folks from Sumeru have come to visit, so we're brainstorming a few nice surprises for them...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Amber!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Ah! Sorry, I... uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Hehehe, at least I didn't say anything about what the surprises are...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Oh nooo, how am I supposed to join this conversation now? What do I say to that...)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Speaking of nice surprises... we've actually had a fairly big one recently.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: What kind of surprise? Tell me! Tell me!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Ahh, I'm saved, Sucrose has given me a lead-in. Now, I just need to follow on from what she's already started talking about...)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sucrose and Collei tell everyone about the "nice surprise" that they've been working on — namely, of course, the prophecy...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Hmm. What an interesting prophecy... I have no idea what the answers could be, though.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: So essentially, you're gathering information to help you solve the riddles, correct? I'll do my best to help.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Eula.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Any time.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: There's no need to answer right away. We'll put a mailbox next to the Crafting Bench for people to drop us a note once they've thought of something.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: I'll drop something in there for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Nice idea, I think we can all commit to writing a note. We'll see what we can come up with.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yep, don't worry, you can count on us! But we do have to finish our patrol first.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: What route are you taking today?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: We started in the Stormbearer Mountains, and we'll end at the city gates. You'd be very welcome to join us, but it sounds like you're pretty busy with all this.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No — there's always next time. We'll join up with you after we're done working through this prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh... yeah, so, um... We'll be on our way for now! Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: See you later! Have a safe trip back.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uhh... was it that obvious?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No, no, not at all. It just looked like you had something on your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ugh, so that means it was obvious... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Whatever's bothering you, you can talk to me about it if you want. I'm happy to help.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Thanks, Sucrose.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Well... the truth is, I don't really know how to act around Amber and the others.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Really? I thought you two were good friends.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: We are... Amber's a really important friend to me...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...I don't know. I guess, if I'm being completely honest, the problem's probably with me...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The first time I came to Mondstadt, I was really immature. I didn't wanna let people in, and I was generally pretty awful to everyone... Amber was the one person who didn't give up on me. If it wasn't for her persistence, I wouldn't have found a friend at all.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Without Amber, I might not even be here today. And because of that, I really look up to her. I think of her as my role model, and hoped that maybe one day, I could learn to be like her...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...But after trying and failing for several years, I think I've finally realized... I'm no Amber, and I never will be.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Looking back, it seems silly that I ever thought like that. We're nothing alike at all... My personality's so... weird. I always get so anxious and I overthink everything...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Aw, Collei... don't say that.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um, Sucrose, would it be okay if I... told you a bit about my past?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: (I already knew bits and pieces about her, but still... Why did she have to go through all that?)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, we've only just met and I'm already dumping all of this on you... This is why I get so frustrated at myself. I'm always doing this... I get into a spiral of self-doubt, and then I end up having to find somewhere to vent it all out...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No no no, it's fine! I—I'm really glad that you're willing to tell me all this.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: People don't open up about their deepest feelings unless they really trust the other person. Don't you think? At least... I think it's kind of an honor.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: And I mean... Umm... You've probably noticed by now, but I don't have the best social skills either. I always just end up talking about the things I'm interested in, and going on and on...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: But even so, you still listen to me when I talk my head off about alchemy. It's a relief to listen to you talking about yourself for once.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: If you hadn't told me all of those things, I never would have guessed that you struggle so much. Honestly, I feel like we're very similar people.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yeah! Everyone has their own problems to deal with... I certainly do!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: All the feelings that you talked about just now... I totally get it. It takes so much more effort for us introverts to fit into a crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: When you were saying about how you try to think about what to say in advance, and you're constantly terrified of saying the wrong thing and making things awkward... I relate to that so much! Oh, and also that part about studying under a genius...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: In fact, before meeting you, I'd never met anyone who seemed so similar to myself.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Um... I'm not very good at giving words of comfort or anything, and I'm not gonna tell you to just get over it or stop worrying about it. How about we just sit here for a little while? We don't have to force a conversation if we can't think of anything. We can just... sit here together.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Sucrose has stopped talking, but for some reason, this doesn't feel awkward at all. Maybe she's right, and we're more similar than I realized.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (In Sumeru, I always like to find a quiet place to just sit and watch the scenery, but it's always by myself. I never thought there'd be a day when I could do this with someone else by my side...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (...Mondstadt's breeze is so gentle and soft.)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hey, Collei... see that cloud over there? Doesn't it look like... one of my test tubes?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um... uh... I don't think so... Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hehe, then maybe we're not quite on the same wavelength on everything... at least, not when it comes to looking at clouds in the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sucrose. I feel much better after talking to you...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yeah, it helps a lot, doesn't it? I also vent to my flasks sometimes. The next time we get the chance, I have to show you my Tetratanic Sweet Flower and my Tetratanic Windblume...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Your Tetra-what??

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Two of my favorite things I've made. They're really cool. I think you might like them.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: O—Oh, okay! Yeah, you'll definitely have to show them to me sometime!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I brought some crackers with me, you want one? There's cheese flavor or tomato flavor.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Sure! Hmm... I'll try the cheese one!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: ...Aw, look! They're enjoying the scenery together!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Shall we go play with them?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: No, it's fine. Let them sit for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: We're not what Collei needs right now. She needs a new friend — someone different, who's never met her before.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: I don't get it... Is there a difference?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: There is! You'll understand once you're a little older, Klee. People can draw different kinds of strength from different kinds of friends, and right now, Collei needs someone that's just not the same ol' me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Starsnatch Cliff, we made it! Paimon hopes we find someone we need here...
Heeeelp! I beg you, please don't let go!
Tsk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's that yelling? Let's hurry and take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Timaeus!? And we also have... Rosaria and Mona!? What kind of mishmash ensemble is this...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Good question. What kind of a motley crew is this?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greetings, everyone. And happy Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You two are looking pretty good. I trust you've been well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep... we're definitely faring a lot better than this poor guy on the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Hey, please don't rub salt in my wound! I really have been trying my best!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You're one to talk! If this sister hadn't grabbed you in time, then you'd have been seriously hurt, if not dead!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I know, I know... I really am grateful, Miss! I can't thank you enough...

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Just lending a hand.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Quite literally. And had she not lent him a hand and pulled him up, he would've gone tumbling down the cliffside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Did Timaeus almost fall off the cliff?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Uh, well... So what actually happened was... I came to Starsnatch Cliff today to pick some flowers, and ran into Mona on the way. She took a look at her scryglass, and advised me to turn back, because it would be dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you still came up here anyway...?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: ...Yes, I did, because there's something I just had to do!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: *sigh* I hardly think giving flowers to your crush is worth throwing one's life away for...

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: It's rare to run into someone with a death wish in this area.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I don't have a death wish! I just... didn't think it would really come true... I mean, when Mona said "it would be dangerous," I thought I'd be fine as long as I watched my step cautiously. I'm sorry, okay? I was wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I'm telling you, I'm just here chasing the love of my life. Lovestruck Mondstadters is what the Windblume Festival's all about!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... That explains you, but why is Rosaria here?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I was looking for a quiet place to escape the crowds. I wasn't planning on having to save a life along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...So that's why the scryglass just showed "danger" instead of "fatal danger."

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: #Ahaha, very funny... Anyway, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, what brings the two of you to Starsnatch Cliff?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just trying our luck! We've got a lot of people we need to see today, so we've been all over the place. Actually, you're some of the people we were looking for!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell them about the prophecy, the information gathered so far, and the mailbox...

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: I see. So all we'll need to do is to find some clues, make a note, and drop it off at the mailbox?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I can't believe there's a prophecy like this... Let alone that I have a part to play in it!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I guess this means everyone will find out about my crush now... Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I came here because I wanted to give some Cecilias to the girl I love. They'll really suit her. She's—

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: No, no, no one asked. Please do not subject us to your gushing about your girlfriend.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Oh... You saw right through me...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You said you need clues, right? In that case, Mona Megistus the Astrologist will provide you with a personally handwritten letter. Just wait for it to show up in your mailbox!

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: You can be on your way, now. We won't keep you any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's head back for now and meet up with everyone else!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bye for now, everyone! Timaeus, please try to stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Will do! Ugh, this is all so embarrassing... Thank you both!

talks.objective: Go to the alchemy crafting bench

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back! Aw, but it looks like you two beat us.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Welcome back! Did everything go well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we managed to find and talk to everybody!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: We got back a little early, so we took some time just now to put the mailbox together.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: We really got lucky today — the vendors were feeling super generous, so we didn't even need to pay for the materials! It's just a shame that Collei got a splinter...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, don't worry about me! I'm used to working in the rainforest — I get splinters all the time. I've already taken care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: We've already wrapped up everything on our to-do list for today, so all we need to do now is wait for everyone's letters to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, why don't you get some rest while I keep an eye on the mailbox?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're definitely your master's student, Sucrose! As long as you or Albedo are around, Paimon can relax and know that everything's taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, stop, you're embarrassing me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, actually, there's one thing that still needs taking care of... Paimon's starving! Hey, Traveler, you wanna get dinner? Your treat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, I guess I'd better go get Paimon some food.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'll go with Sucrose to return the leftover materials to the vendors. You two, go get a proper meal — we can't have anyone going hungry!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yeah, now would be a good time for a break. Once everything is ready, let's meet up here again and collate all the information we've gathered.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon will have this one... And this one, and this one...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hear that? ...It's the sound of Mora pouring out of my wallet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon's really hungry! And don't forget, Paimon's also ordering for you, too. It's not like Paimon's gonna eat everything by herself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! Paimon is super full...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It feels pretty good to just relax and take in the scenery after all that great food.)

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Is everything packed up and ready? What do you think about meeting up at five to go to my house?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Yes, everything's ready. I've packed some great wine and smoked ham — your parents will love it.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Ahem... Ham? Look, we've known each other for quite some time now. Don't you think it's been long enough for you to remember that we only eat bacon in my house?

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Hmm... I must remember to get some milk today on my way home...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Please feel free to pay a visit to Cat's Tail any time.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Enjoying the scenery?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Tone-Deaf Bard! Are you here for some food as well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we order something for you?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oho, I can put something on your tab? Well, that's a pity, I already had a few drinks before coming here.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I shall take you up on your kind offer another day! There should be no shortage of opportunities in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Anywho, you should be getting ready to thank me, I come bearing good news!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What kind of good news?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Behold!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It looks like...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A paper with a simple map and something like an incantation on it.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: It's what you need the most right now — the answer to the prophetic puzzle~

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Simply head to the location marked on the map, and you'll find the lantern you've been looking for. However...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If I were you, I wouldn't just go and reveal the secret right away. As you've seen, a lot of people have been laboring hard to uncover the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: A secret is like a well-aged brew. The aroma from the bottle is sweetest when revealed in the company of friends.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Then it's settled. I'll leave you to your business for now. Feel free to find me for a chat again once you're done working through the prophecy!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, also, if you have some time, we could organize another fast-track love poem class.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're starting that up again?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I sure am! Nobody else has signed up this year though, so the duty to learn falls on you.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Anyway, see you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Venti always looks so relaxed whenever we run into him. Paimon can't help but be jealous...
Excuse me. If you don't mind... could I chat with you for a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: You may call me Scarlett.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Just like you, I'm a traveler, visiting Mondstadt from another land.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Mind if I buy you a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not drinking today. But thank you for offering.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Leaving the door open for another time, I see. I can tell that you've dealt with a lot of people during your travels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can tell? Well, we ARE very experienced adventurers, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: I can. That's why I tried to strike up a conversation with you in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: I was on my way to go shopping earlier when I overheard your conversation next to the Crafting Bench. From what I could gather, you are trying to investigate a bizarre prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Bizarre is definitely the word...

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Don't you think it sounds just like the kind of story that would happen in Mondstadt? Anyway, that's why I wanted to ask you a favor... If and when you manage to unravel the answer to the prophecy, could you let me know what it is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you interested in it too?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: Not so much the prophecy itself, but Mondstadt as a nation. That's what I'm interested in.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: I was born in a distant land, but I have family and friends who once lived in Mondstadt for a long time. They said that it's a great place full of fairytales and romance, and recommended that I come for a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: As it happens, someone I know has an anniversary coming up soon, so I figured this would be a good time to come here and see all the sights that she once saw.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you think about Mondstadt so far?

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: It certainly lives up to its name as the city of romance and freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we think so too!

dialogues.speaker: Scarlett
dialogues.text: So. About the prophecy...

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: Thank you. You're very friendly, it's been a real pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: I'll leave you to it, then. Hope you continue to enjoy the city, and have a wonderful day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She definitely isn't dressed like a local, huh. Where do you think her hometown could be...?

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: "Please find me a flower that is not of this world, and a guide who will never get lost."

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: "Find me one who would never lie, as well as a legend that never ends..."

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: I never thought I'd have someone secretly following me even in a free city like Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Scarlett
response.text: Good day to you, Miss.

choices.text: I'll let you know if we find the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After bidding farewell to Sucrose and Collei...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: At that moment, Sucrose and Collei arrived at Stormbearer Mountains...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: On the other side, the cold winds sing shrill across the face of Starsnatch Cliff...
